Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City DILG OPINION NO. 45 s. 2mo 15 April 2010 MR. TEOPISTO C. ROJAS, JR. SP Member City of Maasin Province of Southern Leyte Dear SP Member Rojas: This is in response to your letter-query seeking the opinion of this Department on the matter concerning the designation of a duly elected Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member as Provincial Administrator. In response thereto, please be informed that we already answered a similar query in DILG Opinion No. 26, series of 2008 where we opined that an elective official is not eligible to be appointed or designated in any capacity to any public office or position in the government during his tenure citing therein Section 94 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160). Attached herewith is a photocopy of the said DILG Opinion for your ready reference. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: AVIV. JESUS B. DOQUEs V Directoöill

Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF UNDERSECREICARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 8 26 14 April 2008 ATTY. ROGELIO U. MARASIGAN Law Department City Hall, Makati City Dear Atty. Marasigan: This pertains to your earlier letter requesting for legal opinion on whether or not Atty. Angel Chona I. Valero, a duly elected Barangay Kagawad of Poblacion, that city, can be appointed as City Legal Officer of Manila. In reply thereto, may we invite your attention to Section 94 (a) of the Local Government Code, which provides: "SEC. 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidates Who Lost in an Election.- (a) NO elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shatt hold any other office or employment in the any subdivision, government or agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporation or their subsidiaries. With the foregoing provision, it is clear that an elective local official is not eligible to be appointed or designated in any capacity to any public office or position in the government during his tenure. We hope to have clarified you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE O Undersecretar Legal/La cc: Atty. Angel Chona l. Valero Barangay Kagawad Poblacion, Makati City
